name: Default Render Layer
description: Default render layer that renders a model with a texture.

fields.description: The model layer to render. Can be a plain model layer like "example:model#main", or an object with a "base" and "variables" to switch between model layers while rendering, the same way dynamic textures do.
The texture to render the model with.
The render type to render the model with.
The light emission of the model. Must be within 0 - 15

Changes the position, rotation or scale of model parts while rendering. Each key is a model part name like "head", a path like "body.cape", or "root" for the whole model. Each part takes a map from "x", "y", "z", "x_rot", "y_rot", "z_rot", "x_scale", "y_scale" or "z_scale" to a MoLang expression. The result replaces the value the part has after copying the pose of the player, and that value is available in the expression as "this". Rotations are in degrees.

Transformation ID(s). The layer only shows while one of these transformations is shown, on the transformed model. Without this field the layer is hidden while a transformation model is shown. Layers inside a compound layer without their own value use the one of the compound.
Skin overlay part(s) that are scaled down slightly while this layer is visible, so they don't stick out of the layer's model. "cape" has no effect.

name: Compound Render Layer
description: Groups several render layers into one. The layers inside only show up while the conditions of the compound itself are met, on top of their own conditions. The model parts in the compound's "hidden_model_parts" are hidden while the compound is visible. Layers inside without their own "transformation" use the one of the closest compound around them that has one.

fields.description: The list of render layers this compound render layer contains.

name: Lightning Sparks
description: Renders lightning sparks around the entity.

fields.description: The frequency of the sparks.
The amount of sparks to spawn during each occurence.
The render settings for the sparks.

Model parts the sparks are limited to, like "right_arm" or "head". Each spark picks one of them and stays inside the box of that part, moving along with it. Nested parts can be written as a path like "body.cape". If none are specified, the sparks fill the whole hitbox of the entity.

name: Cloth Render Layer
description: Renders a simulated cloth grid (a cape by default) that flows, bends and trails behind the wearer instead of turning as one flat plane.

fields.description: Which part of the cloth grid is pinned to the wearer: "back" (cape), "left_arm" or "right_arm" (draped along an arm), or "waist" (skirt or kilt, a box-shaped loop around the hips).
A registered material id (e.g. "argon:heavy") or an inline object overriding individual physics properties.
[length, width] of the cloth at rest, in blocks. For a "waist" attachment, "width" is the half-width of the left and right sides of the box. "depth" sets the front and back.
[segments_x, segments_y]: simulation columns/rows. More = smoother bending at a performance cost.
"back" attachment only. Curves the pinned edge forward so it hugs the wearer's sides, turning a flat cape into a wrap-around cloak. 0 is flat.
"waist" attachment only. Half-depth of the front and back sides, in blocks. Usually smaller than "width", since players are thinner front to back. Defaults to "width".
"waist" attachment only. While crouching, the garment follows the body's pitch as one piece. This scales how much, 0 ignores it and 1 follows fully.
Currently unused. Kept so existing configs that set it still load.
[x, y, z] offset of the attach point from the neck, in wearer space. Y=0 is neck height and higher Y goes down. A cape needs a positive Z to sit behind. For "waist" use X=0, Z=0 and Y about 0.75-0.9.
"back" attachment only. Width at the shoulders as a fraction of the width at the hem, 0.05 to 1. Below 1 the cloth is a trapezoid that flares out to "width" at the hem. 1 is a plain rectangle.

How the cloth reacts to the wearer's real speed, not the selected flight level. Keys: airflow_strength (1), turn_inertia (1), flight_stabilization (0.6, calms swinging at speed), flight_stiffness_multiplier (1.15), stiffness_response (0.1) and body_hug (0.75, how tightly a back cape is pulled against the body near top speed) and hug_start (0.6, how far through the speed range the hugging begins). "narrowing" (not for "waist"): { enabled, start_fraction (0.25) and full_fraction (0.85) of the wearer's top flight speed, start_speed (10 blocks/s) and full_speed (40) when there is no flight, maximum (0.6; 0.35 when "wrap" is above 0 or for arms), compression (0.5, how much of the narrowing squeezes the cloth itself instead of folding it), response (0.06), recovery (0.04), distribution (1.5, higher keeps the top wider), fold (1, 0 turns the pleats off) }. "limb_collision" (back capes): { enabled (true), torso: { width (0.5), depth (0.25), length (1.1), radius (0.1) }, head: { width (0.5), depth (0.5), length (0.5), radius (0.1) }, arms: { radius (0.3), length (0.8) }, legs: { radius (0.25), length (0.8) } }, the shapes the cloth is kept out of. "flutter": { intensity (1), frequency (1), speed_influence (1), damping (0.6), edge_multiplier (1.5) }.
The texture for the cloth. UVs stay stable across the grid however the cloth deforms.
The render type to draw the cloth with.

name: Fade Render Layer
description: Wraps another render layer and draws it at a changing opacity so it can fade in and out. Put the wrapped layer's conditions inside "layer". Nothing is drawn at opacity 0.

fields.description: (Dynamic) 0 to 1, how opaque the wrapped layer is. Usually an ability's eased animation timer, e.g. palladium.get_animation_timer_eased('namespace:power#ability'), which already runs 0 to 1.
The render layer to draw, written exactly as it would be on its own, including its "conditions".

name: Anchored Lightning Sparks
description: Like Palladium's Lightning Sparks, but the sparks can be tied to named body part bones using the same "anchors" as the Thrusters layer.

fields.description: The frequency of the sparks.
How many sparks spawn each time, per anchor (or for the whole entity if "anchors" is empty).
The render settings for the sparks.
Bones to spawn sparks at, e.g. "head" or "right_arm". Each gets its own spark cycle. Empty spawns them anywhere on the entity, like palladium:lightning_sparks.
Only relevant when "anchors" isn't empty: how far, in blocks, sparks jitter from the anchor point.
[x, y, z] offset from the anchor (or the entity if "anchors" is empty), so sparks can sit off the bone's pivot.
